自分の性別を自分でどう認識しているか、という内面の感覚（英語の gender i: An internal sense of how one perceives one's own gender (gender identity in English). Separate from the gender assigned at birth, it refers to the way you feel about your gender. In Japanese, there are three main translations, each with different nuances. "Gender identity" is widely used in the context of human rights and support for people concerned, and also corresponds to "GI" in SOGI. Note that while this term has sometimes been targeted for attack online, it is not the concept itself that is the problem. ``Gender identity'' is a somewhat old translation, and is reminiscent of the old diagnosis ``Gender Identity Disorder'' and the Special Cases Act. "Gender identity" is an expression adopted in the LGBT Understanding Promotion Act of 2023, but it is long and difficult to use in ordinary sentences. Both words refer to the same concept. (Who this word covers is argued over.)

It is also used to express an objection to the existing framework itself. It was originally a derogatory term, but it has been reclaimed by those involved, and is equivalent to the "Q" in LGBTQ+. However, it is still sometimes used in a derogatory manner, and when using it toward someone, it is important to be careful whether the person himself/herself recognizes the word.
